clue.text: Hasten to get around one drunk showing abusiveness

indicators.note: the verb for hurrying is made to encircle the following pieces

parts.note: to hasten is to scurry
one is the Roman numeral I
lit is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Someone rushing round a drunk while showing foul-mouthed hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Scurrility is coarse, abusive language, so the noun matches abusiveness as a synonym.

clue.text: Gesture, as Tom Jones does with name-dropping

indicators.note: the letter for name falls lower down the word, to its end in this down entry

parts.note: Tom Jones is a Welsh singer, so what he does is sing

explanation.surface: A wry remark that Tom Jones's act includes a bit of name-dropping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'name-dropping' looks like the social habit; here it moves the N of SING down to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign is a gesture made to communicate, such as a nod or wave: a direct synonym.

clue.text: Fare for Japanese bus extremely prohibitive, I'd moan regularly

indicators.note: the extremes of the word are banned, leaving only its centre
every other letter of these words is taken

explanation.surface: A grumble that a Japanese bus fare is far too expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' looks like the price of a ticket but means food here.
explanation.definitionFit: Udon are thick wheat noodles, a staple dish of Japanese cuisine, so it is fare eaten in Japan.

clue.text: Pious man on time to join a bishop in recent uprising forming underground network

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher

indicators.note: A and the bishop are placed inside the reversed word
in a down clue, rising means the word for recent is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: new means recent
RR, Right Reverend, is a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A devout man joining a bishop in a recent revolt, forming an underground movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbit warren is a system of interconnected burrows, a literal network of tunnels below ground.

clue.text: Sponge dirty old man with extra energy

indicators.note: the energy letter is added into the middle of the word for a lecher

parts.note: a lech is a lecherous man
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A lecherous old man is a sponger, and a lively one at that.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge in the sense of a parasite who lives off others; a leech is the same kind of hanger-on.

clue.text: Protecting king and earl, junk and vessels participate in rotation

indicators.note: the word for junk surrounds the two title letters as if guarding them

parts.note: tat is cheap rubbish
K is the chess abbreviation for king
urns are vessels

explanation.surface: Junk shielding a king and an earl, with vessels joining in by turns.
explanation.definitionFit: To take turns is to alternate with others, each doing a share in sequence, i.e. rotating.

clue.text: Without resistance, liberated transport route

indicators.note: the resistance letter is left out of the word

parts.note: freed means liberated
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Freed without a fight, with a transport link opened up.
explanation.definitionFit: A feed is a channel or pipe that carries material such as fuel or water to a machine, a supply route.

clue.text: A clean dish might be the result after having cooked that

definitions.text: A clean dish might be the result after having cooked that

indicators.note: cooking here means mixing up letters, so the stated phrase is a reworking of the answer's letters

explanation.surface: After cooking this meal you might be left with a clean plate.
explanation.walkthrough: The logic runs backwards: 'cooked that' means rearranging the answer produces 'A clean dish', so those words are the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Enchiladas are a Mexican dish of rolled stuffed tortillas, which a hungry diner might leave the plate clean after.

clue.text: Get embarrassed over a politician being critical

indicators.note: in a down entry the blushing phrase is turned over, read from the bottom

parts.note: to go red is to blush
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: Someone blushes because a politician is being critical of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Derogatory remarks disparage or belittle, so the adjective is a synonym of critical.

clue.text: Georgia — criminal Rosa Klebb almost escapes from custody

parts.note: GA is the US state abbreviation for Georgia

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are crooked, rearranged
the name loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Rosa Klebb, the Bond villain, as a criminal slipping out of custody in Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaol (British spelling of jail) break is an escape from prison, a plural noun matching escapes.

clue.text: Brand of Christmas card

indicators.note: the answer is formed of letters running through these two words

explanation.surface: Asks what make a particular Christmas card is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brand' suggests a trade name; it means a burn mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand is a mark burned into skin, so a scar is what it leaves; both name a permanent mark.

clue.text: Clobber a Parisian, Roman Catholic reluctant to take part in rearing children

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: the Catholic and reluctant pieces go inside the reversed word
in a down clue, rearing means the word is read upwards

parts.note: seed means offspring
loth means reluctant

explanation.surface: A Frenchman and a reluctant Catholic involved in bringing up children.
explanation.walkthrough: Clobber is British slang for clothes or gear, here used as a noun not the verb 'hit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber is informal British for clothing or kit, and underwear is one kind of garment, a loose fit.

clue.text: Checking how to spell that bloke from The Police

definitions.meaning: checking in the sense of resisting or holding back

definitions.text: how to spell that bloke from The Police

explanation.surface: Checking how to spell the name of a member of the band The Police.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting of The Police: his name is spelt 'with ST and ING', which runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Withstanding means resisting or holding off, as checking an attack does.

clue.text: A myth about car being economical

indicators.note: the myth word goes around the car

parts.note: a fable is a myth
a Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: A fable told about a car's thrifty running.
explanation.definitionFit: Something affordable is within budget, cheap enough, hence economical in price.

clue.text: Female companion lifts old lady with superficial desire

indicators.note: being on the surface, the word for desire lies on the outside of the other pieces

parts.note: a bid is an attempt or wish to obtain
lifts in cars are rides
ma is mother, the old lady

explanation.surface: A woman's friend raises an elderly woman's shallow longing.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridesmaid is a woman attending the bride at a wedding, her companion for the day.

clue.text: With half-hearted server coming at last, get shot of strong drink

indicators.note: the server piece is placed at the end of the answer

parts.note: to get shot of someone is to get rid of them, to fire them

indicators.note: the word loses one of its two central letters, half its heart

parts.note: a waiter serves at table

explanation.surface: A lacklustre waiter turns up late, so you sack him and order a stiff drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Firewater is a colloquial term for strong spirits such as whisky, a fiery liquor.

clue.text: Arrest suspect crossing Yorkshire river, one charged with acquiring loot

indicators.note: the rearranged letters lie across the river name, enclosing it
suspect hints the letters are dubious, to be reshuffled

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Police arrest a suspect crossing a Yorkshire river, charging them over stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged with acquiring loot' sounds criminal; it is the job of looking after an organisation's money.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer is entrusted with an organisation's funds; loot is slang for money.

clue.text: Demand and obtain dismissal to be revoked before court

indicators.note: the reversed word comes ahead of the court letters
revoking turns the dismissal back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the axe means being fired

explanation.surface: A demand that a sacking be overturned before going to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to demand and receive, as in exacting payment or revenge.

clue.text: Stranger died in European river

indicators.note: the died letter goes inside the river's name

parts.note: the Oder flows between Germany and Poland

explanation.surface: A stranger died in a river in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' looks like a noun (an unknown person); it is the comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Odder is the comparative of odd, meaning more peculiar, the same as stranger.

clue.text: Arise achy having broken comfy furniture

indicators.note: the two words are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Getting up stiff and aching after the comfortable seat gave way.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy chair is a large upholstered armchair, a comfortable piece of furniture.

clue.text: Detective without pressure feeling relief

parts.note: DI is Detective Inspector

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the feeling word surrounds the pressure letter

parts.note: a sensation is a feeling
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A detective, freed of pressure, feels relieved.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispensation is an exemption from a rule, a release or relief from an obligation.

clue.text: Love to break mounting depression, showing a benefit of exercise

indicators.note: the zero letter breaks into the reversed word
in a down clue, mounting means the word climbs, reading backwards

parts.note: a dent is a depression
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Love lifting a rising depression, as exercise does.
explanation.definitionFit: Toned muscles are firm and well-defined, a visible reward of working out.

clue.text: Father, one lamenting vocally

indicators.note: the word is said aloud, giving a same-sounding word

parts.note: a sigher is someone who sighs in sorrow

explanation.surface: A father in mourning, voicing his sorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech, sigher and the answer sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To sire is to father offspring, and a sire is a male parent, especially of an animal.

clue.text: Able editor's given up on paper

indicators.note: in a down entry the reversed letters sit on top of the paper
in a down clue, the editor letters are turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor; the 's stands for has
the FT is the Financial Times newspaper

explanation.surface: A capable editor has left the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Deft means skilful and quick with the hands, a synonym of able or adroit.

clue.text: Beast primarily butchered with bladed implement

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: an oar has a blade for rowing

explanation.surface: A beast hacked up with a bladed weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A boar is a wild or male pig, a specific beast.

clue.text: Tore up Brick Lane, going around hot and sticky

indicators.note: the rearranged letters surround the heat letter
tearing up the street name scatters its letters

explanation.surface: Someone tore up Brick Lane, a London street, on a hot and humid day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sticky' suggests humid or gluey; here it means like a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticky read as like a stick: something resembling a twig or bough is shaped like a stick.

clue.text: Goals from two opposing players, defenders gutted

parts.note: in bridge, East and North are opponents of a sort, giving E and N

indicators.note: the word loses its insides, leaving first and last letters

explanation.surface: Goals scored by two players from opposite sides after the defence was torn apart.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are North, South, East and West; E and N sit on different sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Ends are aims or purposes, the goals one is working towards.

clue.text: Seemly to hug son after Irish setter's shot

indicators.note: the main piece follows the Irish and setter letters

parts.note: the setter is I, the clue's author; 's stands for is

indicators.note: the seemly word wraps around the son letter

parts.note: decent means seemly

explanation.surface: An Irish setter, the dog, has been shot, and it seems right to hug its son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish setter' reads as the dog breed; it is IR plus the setter, I.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot as in shot silk: fabric woven so its colour changes with the light, i.e. shimmering.
